newsitem.title: LATVIA: World Bank says satisfied with Latvia progress.
newsitem.headline: World Bank says satisfied with Latvia progress.

text.p: A World Bank mission to Latvia said on Thursday it was satisfied with progress made by the Baltic state under a $60 million structural adjustment loan.
"Latvia has been succesful in maintaining its macroeconomic stability," World Bank economist and head of the mission, Mansour Farsad, told a news conference.
"The rate of inflation is going down on an annual basis and there are signs of economic growth emerging," he added.
He said there were three aspects to the loan, to maintain stability, encourage private sector development and to reform public sector management.
"The mission has noted that the government has been active in promoting financial disclipline, promoting privatisation and improving trade, particularly by reducing tariffs" he added.

The government of Prime Minister Andris Shkele has made the solving of Latvia's economic problems its top priority. It has tried to speed privatisation and introduce fiscal austerity with a planned balanced budget for 1997.
Latvia has already qualified for $20 million of the $60 million loan and is waiting to see if it meets the terms for the further $40 million. It has not drawn on any of the loan.
Farsad said the mission was satisfied with the implementation of a new bankrutpcy law.
He said it made possible the liquidation of some companies and the use of resources where the economy needed them most.
Farsad said the mission was also pleased with the pace of privatisation, which he said was going well and should be complted by mid-1998.
He said that there should be more transparency in some areas of privatisation and advised that Latvia should privatise its energy company Latvenergo in a competitive manner.
Farsad said the mission still had to look into the social assistance and social insurance sectors of the economy.
